issues.finding: Two conclusions are printed as bare membership predicates, '$\in D$' and '$\in E$', although the quantified element is x in the same sentence.
issues.proposed_resolution: Write '$x \in D$' and '$x \in E$' in the two conclusions.

issues.location: using an existence claim and the nonempty-set proof explanation, lines 284 and 305–317
issues.finding: Several inline membership expressions omit their left operand: '$\in A$', '$\in \emptyset$', '$\notin \emptyset$', and '$\notin A$'. The surrounding text specifies either the witness or the quantified element x.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use ordinary prose 'in $A$' for the unnamed object, and write x on the left of membership or nonmembership when the sentence quantifies x.

issues.location: nonempty-set equivalence in the explanatory quote
issues.finding: The conclusion says '$x \neq \emptyset$ iff for some x, x belongs to A', switching from the set A to an element x; the proposition and preceding derivation concern '$A \neq \emptyset$'.
issues.proposed_resolution: State '$A \neq \emptyset$' on the left of the equivalence.

translation_treatment: The Javanese target supplies the missing operands, uses 'in A' prose for the unnamed object, and states nonemptiness of A. A bounded comparison view records each difference; the frozen English bytes remain unchanged.
